regulations.title: BC business entity registration
regulations.summary: Before selling cosmetics under a business name in BC, you need to reserve that name and register your sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation with BC Registry Services.
regulations.regulation_name: Business Corporations Act / Partnership Act - business registration requirements
regulations.authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services
regulations.action_required: Reserve your business name (or confirm you're trading under your own legal name) and complete registration through BC Registry Services before commencing sales.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating and invoicing under an unregistered business name can result in fines and complications remitting taxes or opening a business bank account.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - Sole proprietorships and partnerships

regulations.title: PST registration for cosmetic sales
regulations.summary: Cosmetics are not covered by BC's basic groceries exemption, so they are taxable goods. Sellers must register with the Ministry of Finance and charge 7% Provincial Sales Tax on cosmetic products sold in BC.
regulations.action_required: Register for a PST number with eTaxBC and begin charging 7% PST on cosmetic sales made to BC customers.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling taxable cosmetics without PST registration can lead to retroactive assessment plus penalties and interest under the Provincial Sales Tax Act.

regulations.title: WorkSafeBC employer registration
regulations.summary: If you hire anyone in BC to manufacture, package, or sell your cosmetics, you must register with WorkSafeBC and pay premiums for workers' compensation coverage before they start work.
regulations.action_required: Submit a WorkSafeBC Employer's Registration Application at least 30 days before your first BC employee starts work.
regulations.penalty_note: Employers who fail to register with WorkSafeBC can be assessed unpaid premiums retroactively, plus penalties, and remain personally liable for workplace injury claims.

regulations.title: Packaging and Paper Product producer (Recycle BC) registration
regulations.summary: If you supply packaged cosmetics to BC households (directly, online, or through retailers) and don't qualify for the small-producer exemption, you're a "producer" under BC's Recycling Regulation and must register with Recycle BC to fund and report on recycling of your packaging.
regulations.regulation_name: Recycling Regulation (B.C. Reg. 449/2004), Schedule 5 - Packaging and Printed Paper
regulations.authority: Recycle BC, under the BC Ministry of Environment and Parks' Recycling Regulation
regulations.action_required: Confirm whether you qualify for the small-producer exemption (under $1M BC revenue, under 1 tonne of packaging supplied, or single non-chain retail location); if not, register as a steward with Recycle BC and report your packaging volumes.
regulations.penalty_note: Producers who don't join an approved plan can face enforcement under the Recycling Regulation and Environmental Management Act, including compliance orders and fines.
regulations.source_name: Recycle BC - Are You a Steward?
